name: Government
description: Political concepts, forms and organs of government, constitutions, citizenship, parties, public administration, Nigerian political history and foreign policy, aligned to WAEC, NECO and JAMB.

topics.name: Basic Concepts
topics.summary: The vocabulary of politics: power, authority, influence, legitimacy, sovereignty, state and nation.

subtopics.name: Power, Authority and Influence
subtopics.summary: How power differs from authority and influence, and the types of authority in political life.

objectives.text: Define power, authority and influence
Distinguish power from authority with concrete examples
Describe traditional, charismatic and legal-rational authority

subtopics.name: Legitimacy and Political Culture
subtopics.summary: What makes a government rightful in the eyes of the governed, and how legitimacy is won and lost.

objectives.text: Define legitimacy and explain its importance
Identify the sources and indicators of legitimacy
Explain political socialisation and political culture

subtopics.name: Sovereignty, State and Nation
subtopics.summary: Supreme authority within a territory, its types and limitations, and how a state differs from a nation.

objectives.text: Define sovereignty and list its attributes
Distinguish internal from external and legal from political sovereignty
State the elements of a state and distinguish state from nation

topics.name: Forms and Systems of Government
topics.summary: Who rules and how power is arranged: democracy, monarchy, autocracy, and the presidential, parliamentary, unitary, federal and confederal arrangements.

subtopics.name: Democracy
subtopics.summary: Rule by the people: direct and representative forms, principles, merits and demerits.

objectives.text: Define democracy and distinguish direct from representative democracy
State the principles and pillars of democracy
Evaluate the merits and demerits of democracy

subtopics.name: Monarchy, Aristocracy and Autocracy
subtopics.summary: Non-democratic forms: absolute and constitutional monarchy, aristocracy, oligarchy, totalitarianism and military rule.

objectives.text: Distinguish absolute from constitutional monarchy
Describe aristocracy, oligarchy and totalitarianism
State the features of military rule and its effects on Nigeria

subtopics.name: Presidential and Parliamentary Systems
subtopics.summary: Fused or separated executive and legislature, and how each system works in Nigeria and Britain.

objectives.text: State the features of the presidential system of government
State the features of the parliamentary or cabinet system
Compare the two systems and identify which Nigeria operates

subtopics.name: Unitary, Federal and Confederal Systems
subtopics.summary: How power is shared between the centre and the units, and why states choose each arrangement.

objectives.text: State the features of a unitary system with examples
State the features of a federal system and the reasons for adopting it
Distinguish a federation from a confederation

topics.name: Organs of Government
topics.summary: The legislature, executive and judiciary, the doctrine of separation of powers and the checks each organ holds.

subtopics.name: Separation of Powers and Checks and Balances
subtopics.summary: Montesquieu's doctrine, why it exists, how far it can go and how the organs check one another.

objectives.text: State the doctrine of separation of powers and its origin
Explain checks and balances with Nigerian examples
Evaluate the merits and limitations of the doctrine

subtopics.name: The Legislature
subtopics.summary: Law making, oversight and representation, and the structure of Nigeria's National Assembly.

objectives.text: State the functions of the legislature
Distinguish unicameral from bicameral legislatures
Describe the composition of Nigeria's National Assembly and how a bill becomes law

subtopics.name: The Executive
subtopics.summary: Political and permanent executives, their functions, and the limits placed on executive power.

objectives.text: State the functions of the executive arm of government
Distinguish the political executive from the permanent executive
Describe single, plural, nominal and real executives

subtopics.name: The Judiciary
subtopics.summary: Interpreting the law, judicial review and independence, and the hierarchy of Nigerian courts.

objectives.text: State the functions of the judiciary
Describe the hierarchy of courts in Nigeria
Explain judicial independence, judicial review and the threats to them

topics.name: Constitution and Constitutionalism
topics.summary: The rules that create and limit government: types of constitution, constitutionalism and the rule of law.

subtopics.name: Types of Constitution
subtopics.summary: Written and unwritten, rigid and flexible, unitary and federal constitutions, and their sources.

objectives.text: Define a constitution and state its sources
Distinguish written from unwritten and rigid from flexible constitutions
State the merits and demerits of each type of constitution

subtopics.name: Constitutionalism and the Rule of Law
subtopics.summary: Government limited by law: Dicey's principles, fundamental human rights and the obstacles in practice.

objectives.text: Define constitutionalism and distinguish it from having a constitution
State the principles of the rule of law
Identify fundamental human rights in the 1999 Constitution and limits on them

topics.name: Political Parties, Pressure Groups and Elections
topics.summary: How interests are organised and how citizens choose their rulers.

subtopics.name: Political Parties and Party Systems
subtopics.summary: Functions of parties, one-party, two-party and multi-party systems, and Nigerian party history.

objectives.text: Define a political party and state its functions
Compare one-party, two-party and multi-party systems
Identify the major political parties of the Nigerian republics

subtopics.name: Pressure Groups
subtopics.summary: Interest and promotional groups, their methods, and how they differ from political parties.

objectives.text: Define a pressure group and classify its types
Distinguish a pressure group from a political party
Describe the methods and influence of Nigerian pressure groups

subtopics.name: Elections and Electoral Systems
subtopics.summary: Suffrage, constituencies, electoral systems, electoral bodies and electoral malpractice.

objectives.text: Define election, suffrage and constituency
Compare simple majority, second ballot and proportional representation
State the functions of INEC and identify forms of electoral malpractice

topics.name: Public Administration
topics.summary: The machinery that carries out policy: the civil service, public corporations and local government.

subtopics.name: The Civil Service and Public Corporations
subtopics.summary: Features of the civil service, its functions and problems, and the role of public corporations.

objectives.text: State the features and functions of the civil service
Explain anonymity, neutrality and permanence in the civil service
Describe public corporations, their problems and privatisation in Nigeria

subtopics.name: Local Government
subtopics.summary: The third tier: functions, sources of revenue, the 1976 reform and the problems it still faces.

objectives.text: State the functions and importance of local government
Identify the sources of local government revenue
Explain the 1976 local government reform and current problems

topics.name: Nigerian Government and Politics
topics.summary: From pre-colonial political systems through colonial rule and independence to federalism and the republics.

subtopics.name: Pre-Colonial Political Systems
subtopics.summary: The Hausa-Fulani emirates, the Yoruba kingdoms and the Igbo village republics.

objectives.text: Describe the Hausa-Fulani emirate system of administration
Describe the Oyo and Benin systems of government
Describe Igbo political organisation and compare the three systems

subtopics.name: Colonial Rule and Nationalism
subtopics.summary: Amalgamation, indirect rule, the growth of nationalist movements and the road to independence.

objectives.text: Explain the 1914 amalgamation and the system of indirect rule
Identify the causes and phases of Nigerian nationalism
Name key nationalist leaders and their contributions

subtopics.name: Constitutional Development and the Republics
subtopics.summary: The colonial constitutions, independence, the four republics and Nigeria's federal structure.

objectives.text: Outline the main features of the Clifford to Lyttleton constitutions
Describe the four Nigerian republics and their dates
Explain the growth of Nigerian federalism and its problems

topics.name: Nigeria and the World
topics.summary: Nigeria's foreign policy and the international organisations it belongs to.

subtopics.name: Nigeria's Foreign Policy
subtopics.summary: Objectives, determinants and instruments of Nigeria's foreign policy, with Africa as its centrepiece.

objectives.text: Define foreign policy and state Nigeria's objectives
Identify the determinants and instruments of foreign policy
Explain the Africa-as-centrepiece principle with examples

subtopics.name: International Organisations
subtopics.summary: The United Nations, the African Union and ECOWAS: aims, organs and Nigeria's role in each.

objectives.text: State the aims and principal organs of the United Nations
Trace the OAU to AU transition and state the AU's objectives
State the aims of ECOWAS and Nigeria's role in it

topics.name: Citizenship and Rights
topics.summary: Who a citizen is, how citizenship is acquired, and the rights the 1999 Constitution protects.

subtopics.name: Citizenship
subtopics.summary: Acquisition, loss and duties of citizenship in Nigeria.

objectives.text: Define a citizen and distinguish a citizen from an alien
Explain citizenship by birth, registration and naturalisation
State the duties of a Nigerian citizen

subtopics.name: Fundamental Human Rights
subtopics.summary: Chapter IV rights, limitations, and how they are enforced.

objectives.text: List the fundamental human rights in the 1999 Constitution
Explain how rights may be limited in a democracy
Describe how a citizen can seek redress when rights are violated

topics.name: Nigerian Politics since Independence
topics.summary: Military rule, the return to democracy, and public corporations.

subtopics.name: Military Rule and Democracy
subtopics.summary: Why the military intervened, and how Nigeria returned to civilian rule.

objectives.text: Give reasons for military intervention in Nigerian politics
State features and weaknesses of military rule
Outline the transition programmes that restored democratic rule

subtopics.name: Public Corporations
subtopics.summary: Why governments create corporations, and the case for privatisation.

objectives.text: Define a public corporation and give Nigerian examples
State reasons for establishing public corporations
Discuss problems of public corporations and the argument for privatisation

topics.name: Political Ideologies
topics.summary: The belief systems that shape parties and policy — a standard JAMB topic.

subtopics.name: Capitalism and Socialism
subtopics.summary: Private ownership versus public ownership as organising ideas.

objectives.text: State the main features of capitalism and of socialism
Compare how each system answers the basic economic questions
Give criticisms of each ideology

subtopics.name: Communalism, Fascism and Welfarism
subtopics.summary: African communalism, fascism and the welfare state.

objectives.text: Explain communalism as practised in traditional African societies
State the features of fascism
Define welfarism and give examples of welfare policies

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (as amended)
